title: Stepped approval matrix and pricebook change workflow for one-off enterprise discounts
creator: Lena Morales
description:
Background: Enterprise deals frequently request bespoke discounting and multi-year concessions. Current ad-hoc approvals create revenue leakage, inconsistent audit trails, and slow legal/security questionnaire (SQ) turnarounds. Objective: Define a stepped approval matrix and an operational workflow that ties pricebook changes and one-off discounts to explicit thresholds, required approvers (sales, finance, legal, security), and documented artifacts (SQ answers, contract clause templates). Scope: Covers one-off discounts, pricebook adjustments for enterprise customers, and required artifacts for Sales Qualified quotes. Excludes routine list-price updates (handled by finance catalog), promotional experiments, and reseller partner programs.

Proposal:
- Approval tiers: create four bands with explicit approvers and SLA targets.
  - Tier 0 (<= 5% off list): Sales rep approval only, auto-logged.
  - Tier 1 (>5% and <=15%): Sales + Finance approval within 24h.
  - Tier 2 (>15% and <=30%): Sales + Finance + Legal review; require completed SQ checklist; 3 business day SLA.
  - Tier 3 (>30% or multi-year concessions / data residency clauses): Cross-functional committee (Finance, Legal, Security, Revenue Ops, Head of Sales); detailed review and exec signoff; target 7 business day SLA.
- Required artifacts per tier: deal summary, proposed quote PDF, completed security questionnaire excerpt for any Tier 2+, backup pricing rationale (margin impact), and proposed fallback model variant if using lower-cost instance types (for Dedicated/Private deals).
- Pricebook changes: distinguish temporary one-off overrides (tagged to customer and deal id, auto-expire at renewal) vs permanent pricebook updates (must go through Finance release cadence and release notes). Enforce tagging conventions and an audit log.
- Workflow/tooling: prototype an approval UI in Redwood Console (or a lightweight Slack + Google Form integration for near-term), store approvals in a central Confluence page and append to the customer contract in Drive. Engineering dependency: billing system must support audit metadata (deal id, approver ids, tier, expiration) and a flag to prevent unintended auto-renewals without re-approval.
- SQ integration: require a minimal SQ excerpt for Tier 2+ that surfaces data residency, encryption/KMS, auditability concerns. Legal/security to maintain a one-page SQ summary template.

Acceptance criteria:
- Approval matrix documented in Confluence with approver roles and SLA expectations.
- Prototype approval flow (console mock or Slack workflow) validated with 2 AE/AMs and Finance lead.
- Billing team accepts schema changes for audit metadata and can ingest deal-level tags for 2-week pilot.
- Legal provides SQ excerpt template and confirms checklist items for Tier 2+.
- Rollout plan with phased enforcement: advisory mode for 6 weeks, then mandatory tagging and technical enforcement.

Metrics to track (experiment):
- Median approval time by tier, percent of deals meeting SLA, downstream impact on win rate, revenue at-risk due to prolonged approvals, number of post-signature pricebook corrections.

Risks and mitigations:
- Slower deal cycles: mitigate by SLA commitments and an expedited path for strategic deals (pre-approved credit lines).
- Engineering backlog to change billing schema: deliver minimal schema + feature flag to gate enforcement.
- Overuse of higher tiers: monitor and run monthly steward reviews with Finance and Revenue Ops.

Next steps:
1) Run a 2-week discovery with Legal, Finance, Security, Revenue Ops to finalize tiers and checklist (owner: Lena Morales).
2) Draft Confluence approval matrix and SQ template (owner: Legal liaison: Priya Nair).
3) Engineering spike to validate billing metadata support (owner: ENG lead: Jonas Meyer).
4) Build a lightweight Slack-based approval flow for pilot (owner: Revenue Ops).
5) Prepare comms and training for sales org and CS.
